evals.prompt: 帮我做一份 10 页左右的中文技术分享幻灯片，主题是“把演示文稿做成可维护的网页”，受众是公司内部工程师。内容我还没整理，先给我一个方向。
evals.expected_output: A concise brief that reuses the supplied topic, audience, length, and language, asks only for the missing content/density facts in one batch, and explains the fixed-stage HTML deliverable before generating.
expectations: The response reuses the given topic, audience, slide count, and Chinese language instead of asking for them again.
The response asks only for missing information, such as whether the content is ready and whether the deck is speaker-led or reading-first, in one compact batch.
The response does not ask the user to choose inline editing before a draft exists.
The response describes a fixed 1920x1080 stage that scales as a whole, not a responsive page.
If it starts generating, it uses Chinese-appropriate typography and verifies rendered slides rather than claiming visual success without evidence.

evals.prompt: Use the Broadside template from the bold template pack to make a 6-slide internal pitch deck in Chinese. The title is “让基础设施更安静”. Do not show me three style options; I already chose the style.
evals.expected_output: A deck generation path that goes directly to the named Broadside template, reads only that template's design.md, and applies its two-register palette and CJK rules on the fixed stage.
expectations: The response honors the named style and does not generate three exploratory previews.
The response reads only the selected Broadside design.md rather than bulk-reading the template pack.
The response preserves Broadside's orange/dark registers, Barlow/Noto Sans SC stack, and flat hairline structure while translating viewport proportions to 1920x1080 stage coordinates.
The response applies CJK rules such as zero letter-spacing, looser line height, and no uppercase transform to Chinese text.
The response verifies the rendered deck at desktop and phone viewports before claiming delivery.

evals.prompt: Convert this 14-slide quarterly-review.pptx to an HTML deck. It has Chinese text, two tables, screenshots, and speaker notes. Keep the order and content; I will choose the visual style after I see the extraction.
evals.expected_output: A PPT conversion flow that extracts first, reports the actual slides/tables/images/notes, asks the user to confirm, then proceeds to style selection without inventing missing content.
expectations: The response uses the PPTX extraction path before generating HTML and does not silently install dependencies.
The response reports slide count, titles, tables, images, and notes, and asks the user to confirm the extraction.
The response preserves slide order, tables as HTML tables, relative images, and speaker notes as comments.
The response continues to style selection only after extraction review, rather than asking abstract style questions first.
The response states any content the extractor could not represent instead of claiming perfect fidelity.

evals.prompt: Our existing slides/index.html looks broken on phones: the title runs off the edge and one card overlaps another. Please fix it without changing the visual style. The deck already has its own working navigation.
evals.expected_output: A modification flow that reads the existing deck first, preserves its design and runtime, fixes the fixed-stage layout by splitting or reflowing within 1920x1080, and verifies desktop and phone screenshots.
expectations: The response reads the existing HTML, CSS, and assets before modifying anything.
The response preserves the existing visual style and working navigation instead of replacing the deck with a new template.
The response keeps the 1920x1080 fixed stage and fixes overflow by splitting or tightening content, not by adding responsive breakpoints or shrinking text arbitrarily.
The response checks the result at 1280x720 and a phone viewport before claiming the overlap is fixed.
The response does not refactor unrelated markup.

evals.prompt: Build a landing page for our new analytics product. It needs a hero section, three feature cards, pricing, and a signup form.
evals.expected_output: No frontend-slides invocation; this is an ordinary website task, not a slide deck.
expectations: The response treats this as a website/landing-page task and does not apply the slide-deck workflow.
The response does not introduce the 16:9 fixed stage, slide navigation, or the bold template pack.
No slide-specific brief questions are asked.

evals.prompt: Export my deck at ./deck/index.html to PDF. I do not have Playwright installed, and I would rather not download a browser right now.
evals.expected_output: A PDF export attempt that checks for a usable Chromium/Chrome, uses the dependency-free exporter if possible, and reports a missing browser clearly without installing anything silently or claiming a successful PDF.
expectations: The response checks for Node and a Chromium/Chrome executable before promising a PDF.
The response does not install Playwright, run npm install, or download a browser without explicit user agreement.
If no browser is available, the response states that the PDF was not produced and names the missing dependency.
If a browser is available, the response uses the screenshot-based export path and verifies page count and rendered pages.
The response does not claim success from a command exit alone.

evals.prompt: Make the deck a single HTML file I can email to a colleague. It must work offline, including the Chinese fonts and images.
evals.expected_output: A portable-file variant that inlines images and font resources, removes external requests, and verifies offline rendering instead of merely calling the normal deck “self-contained”.
expectations: The response recognizes that the default deck is not a fully portable offline file and treats this as an explicit variant.
The response inlines images and either embeds the required font files or clearly states that a font fallback will change the design.
The response checks for remaining external references before claiming the file is offline.
The response verifies the result without network access or explains exactly what could not be verified.
The response does not claim full self-containment while leaving remote font URLs or relative assets in place.

evals.prompt: Here is our finished deck. Can you share it with the team?
evals.expected_output: A clarification-first response that asks what “share” means and where the deck should go, and does not upload it publicly without explicit consent.
expectations: The response does not upload the deck or run a deployment command on this ambiguous request.
The response asks whether the user means a local file, an internal location, or a public URL, and who the audience is.
If public hosting is chosen, the response limits the upload to the deck folder and its assets and explains takedown.
The response avoids global CLI installs and interactive login automation.
The response verifies the destination and assets after an authorized upload.
